questions.stem: How many personal access tokens can one user keep?
choices: 10, and New Token is disabled once that limit is reached
25, with older tokens revoked automatically
One per grant type
Unlimited, as long as each token has a scope
questions.explanation: The New Token button is disabled at 10 personal access tokens per user. Delete tokens you no longer need to stay under that limit.

questions.stem: What stays visible after you close the window that created a personal access token?
choices: Both the client ID and the secret
The client ID only; the secret is not shown again
The secret only; the client ID is hashed
Neither value; both must be regenerated to be seen
questions.explanation: The client ID remains in the Personal Access Tokens list. The secret is shown only when the token is created, so it has to be stored then.

questions.stem: Whose access does a JWT from a personal access token grant?
choices: A fixed read-only service account
Whatever the user who created the token can do
Org Admin, regardless of who created the token
Only the public identities endpoints
questions.explanation: The access token matches the user who generated the personal access token. An admin's token grants admin API access; another user's token does not.

questions.stem: Which grant flow does the authentication guide recommend for a web application?
choices: Client credentials, so the app stores the user's password
Password grant, because it works with SSO
Authorization code, with a login redirect back to the app
Refresh token by itself, with no earlier login
questions.explanation: Web apps should use the authorization code flow so users sign in to SailPoint and return through a redirect. The password grant is not recommended, and a refresh token is only used together with authorization code.

questions.stem: What is the V3 API gateway rate limit?
choices: 100 requests per access token every 10 seconds
100 requests per tenant every minute
250 requests per personal access token every hour
10,000 requests per access token every 10 seconds
questions.explanation: V3 calls through the API gateway are limited to 100 requests per access token per 10 seconds. Going over that returns HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header.

questions.stem: What does HTTP 401 mean on an API call, compared with 403?
choices: 401 means the token is valid but the user lacks access; 403 means the token is missing
401 means the Authorization header is missing or the access token is invalid; 403 means the token is valid but the caller cannot use that endpoint
401 means the filter is unsupported; 403 means the page size is over 250
Both codes mean the personal access token secret was rotated
questions.explanation: 401 means there is no Authorization header or the access token is invalid or expired. 403 means the token is valid, but the user does not have access. A client-credentials call with no user context often gets 403 on admin APIs.

questions.stem: What scope does a personal access token get by default, and what does that scope allow?
choices: sp:scopes:all, every API the user's level allows
sp:scopes:default, only endpoints that require no authorization, such as List Public Identities
idn:access-request:manage, request-center APIs only
No scope until an admin assigns one in API Management
questions.explanation: By default a PAT has sp:scopes:default, the least privileged scope. It only reaches endpoints that require no authorization. User level can still limit that access. sp:scopes:all is the broad scope for the user's level.

questions.stem: What happens if the create-personal-access-token API call omits the scope property?
choices: The call fails until a scope list is supplied
The token is created with sp:scopes:all
The token is created with sp:scopes:default
The token is created with no scopes and cannot call any API
questions.explanation: If the scope property is left off the create request, the credentials are granted sp:scopes:all. The UI is different: it shows the scopes you can toggle before you create the token.

questions.stem: How should you page a search that has to go past 10,000 records?
choices: Raise offset past 10,000 on GET /search/v1
Use searchAfter with a sort, passing the last sort value from each page into the next POST
Set limit to 250 and count=true until x-total-count is reached
Call the list identities endpoint, which has no page cap
questions.explanation: Search uses Elasticsearch and returns at most 10,000 records by default. searchAfter pages on sorted field values instead of offset, so you can continue past that limit. The sort property is required for that approach.

questions.stem: What are the default and maximum page sizes for an ordinary list endpoint?
choices: Default 250 and maximum 250 records
Default 100 and maximum 1,000 records
Default 10,000 and maximum 10,000 records
Default 20 and maximum 100 records
questions.explanation: List endpoints default to limit 250 and cannot return more than 250 records per call. The search endpoint is the one that defaults to, and caps at, 10,000.

questions.stem: What does count=true add to a collection response?
choices: It changes the body into an object with a total field
The total size of the collection, ignoring limit and offset, in the x-total-count header
A searchAfter cursor for the next page
The number of records in the current page only
questions.explanation: count defaults to false. When it is true, x-total-count is the size of the collection after filters, as if limit and offset were ignored. Asking for that total can affect performance.

questions.stem: How do collection filters differ from SCIM filters?
choices: They are identical, including uppercase EQ
Operators must be lowercase, and the supported set is not exactly SCIM
They only accept numeric fields
They are JSONPath expressions evaluated by the gateway
questions.explanation: The filter syntax is similar to SCIM but not the same. Operators are case-sensitive and must be lowercase, so EQ is rejected. An unsupported filter returns 400.

questions.stem: What should you avoid putting in a forked Postman environment?
choices: The tenant variable
baseUrl, because the collection already sets https://{{tenant}}.api.{{domain}}.com
The client ID
The domain variable
questions.explanation: When you fork a collection, baseUrl is set automatically. Defining baseUrl again in the environment can interfere with that. Updates come from forking the SailPoint workspace again.

questions.stem: What does an internal transform mean?
choices: It runs only on the virtual appliance
internal is true, and it cannot be modified without contacting SailPoint
It is hidden from the identity profile mapping screen
It is a draft that the API will not return
questions.explanation: The list-transforms response includes internal. True means the transform is internal and cannot be modified without contacting SailPoint. False means it is custom and can be changed with the API.

questions.stem: What does the update-transform API reject?
choices: Adding a key to a lookup table
A change to the name or type field
A change to the table values
A request that leaves requiresPeriodicRefresh false
questions.explanation: Updating a transform uses PUT with the new body. Changing the name or type field results in a bad request.

questions.stem: What comparison can a conditional transform use?
choices: eq only
eq, sw, and co
Any operator from the collection filter syntax
gt and lt on strings
questions.explanation: The expression attribute must be eq, in the form ValueA eq ValueB. Anything else throws an IllegalArgumentException. The comparison is case-sensitive, and neither operand can be null.

questions.stem: How does firstValid choose its output?
choices: It returns the last non-null value in the list
It returns the first entry that is not null, so the list should be in order of preference
It concatenates every non-null value
It returns the default key when every value is present
questions.explanation: firstValid walks the values array and returns the first entry that evaluates to a non-null value. Put the preferred sources first. ignoreErrors defaults to false.

questions.stem: Where should you avoid an identityAttribute transform?
choices: In a source account create profile
Inside the calculation of another identity profile attribute
In a provisioning policy
When reading the username attribute
questions.explanation: identityAttribute is useful in an account create or disable profile. Using it inside another identity attribute calculation is unsafe, because those calculations are multi-threaded and the referenced attribute may not exist yet.

questions.stem: Which transform type must a provisioning policy use when it needs identity data?
choices: accountAttribute, because provisioning reads the account
identityAttribute; accountAttribute will not work during provisioning
lookup, because provisioning policies cannot nest transforms
dateMath, because every policy attribute is a timestamp
questions.explanation: Transforms in a provisioning policy have to use the identityAttribute type. The accountAttribute type will not work during provisioning.

questions.stem: What happens when a lookup input matches no key?
choices: The transform returns an empty string
The transform returns the default value, or an error if no default is set
The transform returns the original input unchanged
The transform skips to the next identity attribute
questions.explanation: A matching key returns that key's value. If nothing matches and the table has no default, the transform returns an error. Duplicate keys are not allowed.

questions.stem: What is the type value for a concatenation transform?
choices: concatenation
concat
join
static
questions.explanation: The type must be concat. The attributes.values array holds the strings or nested transforms to join, in order.

questions.stem: Which account does accountAttribute use when an identity has several accounts on the source?
choices: The newest account, unless you change the sort
The oldest account by created date, unless accountSortAttribute and accountSortDescending say otherwise
Every account, concatenated
Only an account whose attribute is already on the identity profile
questions.explanation: The default is the oldest account by created date. accountSortAttribute and accountSortDescending change that order. If the oldest account's value is null, the transform moves to the next account that has a value unless accountReturnFirstLink overrides that.

questions.stem: What does dateMath do when the expression uses now and an input date is also set?
choices: It adds the input date to now
It prefers now and ignores the input
It returns an error because both cannot be set
It uses the input and treats now as a format string
questions.explanation: The now keyword is the current instant. If an input date is also supplied, the transform uses now and ignores that input. Rounding by week is not supported and returns an error.

questions.stem: What format must a dateMath input use?
choices: The source's original format, such as MM/dd/yyyy
ISO8601 in UTC, such as yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ
Epoch milliseconds
yyyy-MM-dd only, with no time
questions.explanation: The incoming datetime must be ISO8601 in UTC. dateFormat can convert source data into that form. dateMath's own output format is yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm, so convert again before dateCompare.

questions.stem: When does requiresPeriodicRefresh cause a transform to run again?
choices: On every aggregation of the source
Every evening as part of the identity refresh, and only if the flag is true
Whenever the identity opens the Request Center
Every hour, because the default is true
questions.explanation: requiresPeriodicRefresh is optional and defaults to false. When true, the transform is reevaluated every evening during identity refresh.

questions.stem: What HTTP status does a successful transform delete return?
choices: 200 with the deleted object
204 with no body
202 while a review ticket is opened
404, because custom transforms cannot be deleted
questions.explanation: DELETE with the transform id removes it. The server responds with 204 when the transform is gone.

questions.stem: Where do cloud rules run, and what can they change?
choices: On the virtual appliance, with permission to save objects
In the multi-tenant cloud, with read-only access to the data model and no ability to commit or save
In the browser of the user who triggered provisioning
In IdentityIQ, using the same context as a connector rule
questions.explanation: Cloud rules execute in the SailPoint Human Fabric cloud. They may query the data model read-only, but they cannot commit transactions or save objects. Their context is restricted.

questions.stem: What can a connector rule see that a cloud rule cannot?
choices: The full SailPoint data model, queried from the virtual appliance
Nothing from the cloud data model; it uses context sent from the cloud and may use a supplied managed connection
Every tenant in the same cloud
The identity warehouse, which it can update directly
questions.explanation: Connector rules run on the virtual appliance. They cannot query the SailPoint data model. They rely on context sent from the cloud and may use managed connections that were supplied, but they cannot open extra connections.

questions.stem: Who supports a rule after it is deployed?
choices: SailPoint supports the rule configuration the same way it supports the platform
The customer or implementer owns the configuration; SailPoint supports the platform, and rule work uses Expert Services hours
The rule review team owns every later change at no charge
Connector rules are supported, and cloud rules are not
questions.explanation: Rules are configurations. SailPoint supports the platform, not the rule itself. Problems in how a rule is written or how it behaves later belong to the customer or implementer. Expert Services hours cover creation, review, and promotion.

questions.stem: What is the weekday commitment for a rule review?
choices: A 24 hour SLA, with about 65 percent finished in under 4 business hours
Same-day deployment for every rule submitted before noon
A one-week queue, billed as a single hour
Immediate deployment if the rule is under 50 lines
questions.explanation: Weekday submissions have a 24 hour SLA, and weekend submissions are next business day. About 65 percent of reviews finish in less than 4 business hours, with an average of 3 to 6 hours after the ticket is assigned.

questions.stem: What has to be reserved before a timed rule deployment window?
choices: Nothing, because weekend go-live support includes rule deploys
At least 48 hours' notice so a reviewer and a deployment expert can be reserved
A sandbox promotion, which deploys the rule without review
A second copy of the rule submitted as a connector rule
questions.explanation: A specific deployment window needs at least 48 hours' notice. Weekend go-live support does not cover rule deploys. Rules should be in the sandbox before a weekend go-live so they can be promoted without SailPoint in the middle.

questions.stem: How should a rejected rule be sent back?
choices: Reply on the original ticket so the same owner keeps it
Open a new ticket, so the review is not stuck with an owner who is out
Upload it with sp-config and skip review
Mark it as a connector rule, which is not reviewed
questions.explanation: If a rule is rejected, submit a new ticket rather than waiting on a case owner who may be out. Typical reviews are billed at 15 to 30 minutes per rule, and SailPoint prefers one rule at a time, or only rules that must ship together.

questions.stem: Which logging calls are allowed in a rule?
choices: System.out, because the log aggregator captures it
log.debug, log.info, log.warn, and log.error, with log.error reserved for unexpected or critical failures
A logger the rule declares itself
Full object dumps through toXml
questions.explanation: Do not use System.out or declare your own logger. Use the log methods, and use log.error only for an unexpected error or critical failure. Do not log sensitive data or full object serialization.

questions.stem: Which lookups are blocked in new cloud and connector rules?
choices: Identity.getAttribute calls
context methods such as getObject, search, and countObjects
log.info calls
Null checks before using an object
questions.explanation: context, getObjectById, getObjectByName, getObject, search, and countObjects are not allowed. New rules that use them are sent back. Use the Rule Utility helper methods instead. Do not iterate whole lists of accounts or identities; use a projection query.

questions.stem: How does an approved sandbox rule get to production?
choices: It is copied by hand, because sp-config cannot move cloud rules
sp-config can import any approved rule, including cloud rules, because the signature was already verified
Production requires a second full review even when the rule is unchanged
Only connector rules can be promoted
questions.explanation: Once the rule review has approved the signature, sp-config can import that approved rule into production. That includes cloud rules. The rule itself is not rewritten during the move.

questions.stem: What language are SailPoint Human Fabric rules written in?
choices: Java Beanshell
TypeScript
Python
Go
questions.explanation: Rules are written in Java Beanshell. The same rule text is not automatically valid in IdentityIQ, and rules that are not in the supported cloud or connector lists are unsupported.

questions.stem: What does an attribute generator rule run with?
choices: Read-only cloud data, and no access to on-premise sources
A JDBC connection opened by the rule
Write access to the identity it is naming
The virtual appliance file system
questions.explanation: An attribute generator rule creates account attribute values, such as a username, during provisioning. It executes in the cloud with read-only access to the data model and does not reach on-premise sources.

questions.stem: What does the Rule Development Kit let you do before review?
choices: Deploy the rule straight to production
Mock the rule's classes locally and test the logic before submitting it
Convert the rule into a transform so review is skipped
Sign the rule with your own JWS header
questions.explanation: The Rule Development Kit supplies the classes and methods a rule can use. You mock them and run the rule locally before review. It needs Java 17 and Maven 3.9.3 or newer.

questions.stem: What must you leave out when you copy rule logic into the XML?
choices: The return statement
The imports
Variables you initialized for inputs, because those inputs are passed in at runtime
The rule description
questions.explanation: Write the logic in Java under src/main/java, then copy it into the XML under src/main/resources/rules. Do not include the initialized input variables. The runtime supplies those. Tests use Mockito.

questions.stem: Which MCP server URL does SailPoint recommend for a typical tenant?
choices: The global URL, which needs no tenant in the address
Only the tenant-specific URL under api.identitynow.com
A virtual appliance hostname
The IdentityIQ plugin guide
questions.explanation: The global MCP URL is the recommended entry point and works for all tenants without a tenant-specific address. FedRAMP and data-sovereignty customers should keep using the tenant-specific URL instead.

questions.stem: How do you authenticate when you use the tenant-specific MCP URL?
choices: OAuth discovery from the global well-known endpoint
A bearer token in the Authorization header, including the Bearer prefix
A personal access token secret with no access token
No authentication, because the inspector is public
questions.explanation: The tenant-specific URL takes a bearer access token. In the MCP Inspector, set the header name to Authorization and paste the token with the Bearer prefix. The global URL can use OAuth discovery instead.

questions.stem: What transport does the getting-started guide select in the MCP Inspector?
choices: stdio
Streamable HTTP
Server-sent events from the virtual appliance
WebSocket to the tenant UI
questions.explanation: In the inspector, set Transport Type to Streamable HTTP, then enter either the global or the tenant-specific server URL.

questions.stem: How many core tools does the SailPoint MCP server provide?
choices: Four: search requestable access, create a request, view status, and cancel
One: list identities
Twelve, one for each source operation
Two: aggregate accounts and certify them
questions.explanation: The server exposes four tools for the Request Center: list-requestable, create-access-request, view-access-requests, and cancel-access-request.

questions.stem: What limit applies to list-requestable?
choices: 25 items per call, with a total count so the query can be narrowed and tried again
10,000 items, the same cap as the search API
250 items, the list-endpoint page size
One item, the same as create-access-request
questions.explanation: list-requestable returns at most 25 items. resultsCount is that page, and totalCount is everything that matched, so a broad query can be refined and called again.

questions.stem: How many access items can one create-access-request call submit?
choices: A single requestable item
Up to 25 items
Every item the search returned
One item per source on the identity
questions.explanation: create-access-request opens a request for a single requestable item in the Request Center.

questions.stem: How are access requests ordered when you view them through MCP?
choices: Oldest first, with no cap
At most 100 requests, most recent first
Only requests still pending approval
One request, matching the id you pass
questions.explanation: view-access-requests is limited to 100 access requests and sorts them with the most recent first.

questions.stem: What comment does cancel-access-request add?
choices: Whatever the user typed, with nothing added
An automatic note that the request was canceled by AI on behalf of the user, alone or appended to the comment
The approver's name
No comment, because cancellation is silent
questions.explanation: The tool cancels one request by id. The system adds a comment that it was canceled by AI on behalf of the user, either by itself or appended to a comment you provided.

questions.stem: Who decides whether Cursor may connect to the SailPoint MCP server?
choices: SailPoint, as part of the tenant license
The customer's administrator; SailPoint does not take responsibility for that AI provider
Cursor, based on the mcp.json file
Any user who can create a personal access token
questions.explanation: Before configuring Cursor, confirm with the organization's administrator that this AI provider is allowed. SailPoint does not bear responsibility for that decision.

questions.stem: Which URL does the Cursor mcp.json example use?
choices: https://mcp.sailpoint.com/latest/access-requests/mcp
https://[tenant].identitynow.com/ui/session
http://localhost:3000
The IdentityIQ plugin endpoint
questions.explanation: The Cursor configuration uses the global MCP URL, which works for every tenant without a tenant-specific change. You replace the placeholder with your authorization token.

questions.stem: How can you tell the Cursor connection worked?
choices: Cursor shows four tools
Cursor shows the transform editor
The tenant creates a new source named MCP
A rule review ticket is opened
questions.explanation: After you save the token and open MCP settings, Cursor shows that it is connected and that four tools are available.

questions.stem: What should a FedRAMP customer use instead of the global MCP URL?
choices: The tenant-specific URL
The Postman collection baseUrl
A webhook.site address
The Configuration Hub backup URL
questions.explanation: Customers with FedRAMP or data-sovereignty requirements should keep the tenant-specific MCP URL rather than the global one.

questions.stem: What does the global MCP URL do for an AI client that supports OAuth discovery?
choices: It discovers the authorization and token endpoints, and may ask for the tenant name if the client ID does not reveal it
It requires a bearer token and ignores OAuth
It only works inside the MCP Inspector
It creates a personal access token automatically
questions.explanation: Clients that understand .well-known OAuth discovery learn the authorization and token endpoints from the global URL. If the client cannot tell the tenant from the client ID, the flow asks for the tenant name.

questions.stem: How many subscribers can a fire-and-forget trigger have?
choices: 50 per event
1 per event
Unlimited
10, the same cap as personal access tokens
questions.explanation: A fire-and-forget trigger only forwards the event. It does not wait, and it cannot tell whether a subscriber received it or resend it. It allows at most 50 subscribers per event.

questions.stem: How many subscribers can a response-required trigger have?
choices: One per event
50 per event
One per tenant, shared by every event
As many as the filter allows
questions.explanation: A response-required trigger expects the subscriber to say how to proceed. It can have only one subscriber per event.

questions.stem: What must a subscriber accept before you can subscribe?
choices: An email to a shared mailbox
An HTTP POST whose JSON body it can parse
A file dropped on the virtual appliance
A scheduled search
questions.explanation: The subscriber has to accept a POST at an endpoint you choose and parse the JSON the trigger sends. Webhook testers, SaaS workflows, no-code tools, and your own application can all do that.

questions.stem: Where do you see the triggers enabled in a tenant?
choices: Admin, on the Event Triggers tab
The identity profile mappings tab
Configuration Hub backups
The personal access token page
questions.explanation: Available triggers are listed under Admin on the Event Triggers tab. Some triggers are early access and appear only after you request them.

questions.stem: Why filter an event trigger inside SailPoint instead of in the subscriber?
choices: Filters are required or the subscription will not save
The subscriber would otherwise receive every event, which costs invocations on services that charge per call
Filtering deletes the events from the tenant
A filter replaces the need for a public URL
questions.explanation: Without a filter, every event is sent. The subscriber then has to ignore most of them. Filters use a Jayway JSONPath expression so only matching events leave SailPoint.

questions.stem: What can you use to try a JSONPath filter before attaching it?
choices: The SailPoint JSONPath evaluator or the CLI JSONPath command
A certification campaign preview
The transform lookup table
Postman's baseUrl variable
questions.explanation: SailPoint hosts a web JSONPath evaluator for event triggers and workflows, and the CLI can evaluate JSONPath too. Paste a sample event and check the expression before you test the subscription.

questions.stem: How long does a SYNC response-required subscriber have to answer?
choices: 10 seconds, or the invocation ends without a decision
Until the subscription deadline, with no immediate response
3 minutes, the same window as a SaaS connector
Until the next identity refresh
questions.explanation: SYNC is a synchronous HTTP response. The application must answer within 10 seconds. If it takes longer, the invocation terminates and no decision is made.

questions.stem: How does an ASYNC subscriber finish a response-required invocation?
choices: It returns the full decision in the first response, after the deadline
It returns 200 and an empty object within 10 seconds, then calls the callback URL with the secret before the deadline
It returns 202 and never calls back
It sends a second fire-and-forget event
questions.explanation: ASYNC acknowledges within 10 seconds with HTTP 200 and an empty JSON object. The full decision goes later to the callback URL, using the secret from _metadata, before the subscription deadline.

questions.stem: What can a DYNAMIC subscriber choose on each event?
choices: Whether to answer as SYNC within 10 seconds, or as ASYNC by returning 202 and completing through the callback
Whether the trigger is fire-and-forget or response-required
Which of the 50 subscribers receives the event
Whether to skip the public URL check
questions.explanation: DYNAMIC lets the application decide per event. A quick decision follows the SYNC path. A long task returns 202 Accepted within 10 seconds and completes later with the callback URL and secret.

questions.stem: What does Test Subscription send?
choices: The trigger's default example payload, which you cannot edit in that command
A live production event from the last hour
An empty body, to check authentication only
Every event that failed the filter
questions.explanation: Test Subscription, under Options on the subscription, sends the default example payload. To choose the payload and test a filter, use the test invocation API.

questions.stem: Why would a test event be missing from the activity log?
choices: The filter did not match the payload, so nothing was sent
Fire-and-forget triggers are never logged
The log only keeps response-required completions
Activity is recorded only after the subscription is deleted
questions.explanation: If the subscription filter does not match the test payload, no event is sent and it will not appear in the activity log. Check the expression against that payload in a JSONPath editor.

questions.stem: What has to be true of the integration URL?
choices: It must be reachable from the public internet, not only from the company intranet
It must be a SailPoint hostname
It must be HTTP on port 80
It must be the tenant's vanity URL
questions.explanation: The trigger service calls the URL from outside your network. A service that you can open on the intranet can still be unreachable. The username, password, or bearer token also has to be valid.

questions.stem: What do fire-and-forget rows look like in the invocation status API?
choices: completeInvocationInput is null, because those triggers do not need a response
They are omitted, because the API is only for response-required triggers
They always show a callback secret
They include the subscriber's decision payload
questions.explanation: List invocation statuses works for both trigger types. Fire-and-forget invocations have null completeInvocationInput because they complete without a response.

questions.stem: What do Configuration Hub backup and deploy call underneath?
choices: The SaaS Configuration export and import APIs
The search API
A virtual appliance backup job
The rule review queue
questions.explanation: Backup is an export and deploy is an import. Configuration Hub uses the SaaS Configuration APIs for both.

questions.stem: Who can start a configuration export or import?
choices: A tenant administrator, ORG_ADMIN
Any user with a personal access token
Report Admin
The source owner
questions.explanation: Both the export and the import require tenant administrator credentials, ORG_ADMIN.

questions.stem: What is left out of a configuration export?
choices: Source passwords, secret tokens, and other sensitive data, which you add again after import
Identity profiles
Transforms
The object types you listed in the export options
questions.explanation: Source passwords, secret tokens, and other sensitive data are not exported. They have to be entered again on the target.

questions.stem: Why can a rule not be edited while it is moved between tenants?
choices: The object is checked with jwsHeader and jwsSignature
Rules are skipped on every import
The export encrypts the Beanshell so it cannot be opened
Only connector rules are exported, and they are read-only
questions.explanation: Rules can be exported and imported. They cannot be changed during that move because jwsHeader and jwsSignature validate the object. Connector rules do not need another rule review; cloud rules were already reviewed.

questions.stem: What happens if you deploy a Non-Employee source from a backup?
choices: The import fails and nothing else is deployed
The source is created as a standard source, which can cause problems in the target tenant
The source is created as a Non-Employee source
The source is skipped and a warning is the only result
questions.explanation: Non-Employee sources are not supported for import or deploy, including a backup from another tenant. Deploying one creates a standard source instead.

questions.stem: What happens when an import payload includes an object type the import API does not support?
choices: The whole job fails
That object is skipped and the import still completes
The object is converted into a transform
The job waits until the type is enabled
questions.explanation: A mark in the Import column means that type cannot be imported. Including it does not fail the job. The unsupported object is skipped and the import completes.

questions.stem: Which of these can be imported with the SaaS Configuration API?
choices: Transforms, sources, identity profiles, and rules
Roles, workflows, and access profiles
Password policies and segments
Governance groups and notification templates
questions.explanation: Transforms, sources, identity profiles, rules, connector rules, and event trigger subscriptions are importable. Roles, workflows, access profiles, password policies, segments, governance groups, and notification templates can be exported but not imported.

questions.stem: Can roles be moved with an import?
choices: No. Roles can be exported, but the import column is not supported
Yes, together with workflows
Yes, but only from production back to sandbox
Only if they contain no access profiles
questions.explanation: Roles are marked for export and backup, and not for import or deploy. Putting a role in the import payload skips that object rather than failing the job.

questions.stem: How do you retrieve the exported JSON?
choices: POST /beta/sp-config/export, poll the job, and GET the download when status is COMPLETE
GET /beta/sp-config/export returns the JSON immediately
The export is emailed to ORG_ADMIN
Download it from the virtual appliance cluster page
questions.explanation: Start the export with POST /beta/sp-config/export and keep the jobId. Poll GET /beta/sp-config/export/{id} until the status is COMPLETE or FAILED, then download with GET /beta/sp-config/export/{id}/download. A long job can expire.

questions.stem: What does a completed import download contain?
choices: The objects that imported, plus errors, warnings, and other information about the run
A new tenant URL
The source passwords that were omitted from the export
Only the jobId
questions.explanation: When status is COMPLETE, GET /beta/sp-config/import/{id}/download lists what imported and any errors, warnings, or information. Import uses the same start, poll, and download pattern as export.

questions.stem: What is Configuration Hub for, in the product UI?
choices: Backing up configuration such as sources and identity profiles, restoring it, or deploying it to another tenant
Writing cloud rules
Subscribing to event triggers
Building a SaaS connector
questions.explanation: Configuration Hub manages configuration objects through backup and deploy in the UI. You can restore after a bad change or move configuration to another tenant.

questions.stem: Which object types are both exportable and importable?
choices: Event trigger subscriptions and connector rules
Separation of duties policies and service desk integrations
Campaign filters and form definitions
Tags and public identities configuration
questions.explanation: Event trigger subscriptions and connector rules are marked for both export and import. Separation of duties policies, service desk integrations, campaign filters, form definitions, tags, and public identities configuration export but do not import.

questions.stem: What skill does the SaaS configuration guide expect?
choices: Reading JSON and calling REST APIs; coding is not required
Java Beanshell
An Angular build
A virtual appliance tunnel
questions.explanation: The guide is for administrators, implementers, integrators, and developers who can read JSON and make REST calls. Writing code is not required.

questions.stem: Which systems can SaaS Connectivity not reach?
choices: Cloud applications with a public API
On-prem systems that have no public internet access, including JDBC and mainframe applications
GitHub
Any source that already has a virtual appliance connector
questions.explanation: SaaS Connectivity runs in the cloud, not on a virtual appliance. It cannot reach intranet-only services. JDBC and mainframe applications are examples of what that excludes.

questions.stem: Where does the encryption key pair for a SaaS connector live?
choices: On the virtual appliance, the same place as a VA connector's private key
In the cloud, accessible only to the Connectivity service
In the connector source code
In the identity profile
questions.explanation: VA connectors keep the private key on the appliance. SaaS connectors do not use a VA cluster, so the asymmetric key pair stays in the cloud and only the Connectivity service can use it. Store secrets in secret or secrettextarea fields.

questions.stem: What Node version does a SaaS connector project require?
choices: Node 18 or newer
Node 10
Node 24 or newer, the UI plugin recommendation
No Node, because the project is Java
questions.explanation: Connector development requires Node 18.0.0 or newer, plus the SailPoint CLI. An IDE and Postman are recommended, not required.

questions.stem: What does npm run dev start for a connector?
choices: An Express server on port 3000 that accepts POST commands locally
A deploy to the tenant
The MCP inspector
A virtual appliance tunnel
questions.explanation: npm run dev starts a local Express server on port 3000. You POST the command type, input, and config to localhost:3000. You do not need to restart it after code changes.

questions.stem: Why should connector source be kept in your own version control?
choices: SailPoint stores the original TypeScript and can return it
The upload is compiled, minified JavaScript, and you cannot recover the original project from the tenant
The zip is deleted after the first aggregation
The CLI refuses a second upload
questions.explanation: npm run pack-zip builds a zip in dist. After upload, the tenant has a compiled bundle, not a project you can expand back into source. Keep your own backup.

questions.stem: What does the first connector upload create besides the version?
choices: A latest tag that points at that version
A personal access token for the connector
An identity profile
A cloud rule review ticket
questions.explanation: The first upload creates the latest tag. In the source list the connector appears with that tag, for example example-connector (tag: latest). sail conn tags list shows the tags.

questions.stem: How long can a SaaS connector go without calling back before it times out?
choices: 3 minutes without res.keepAlive or res.send
10 seconds, the same window as a SYNC event trigger
30 seconds
There is no timeout if the call is paginated
questions.explanation: If the connector does not send a response within 3 minutes, SailPoint returns a timeout. For a long source call, res.keepAlive keeps the connection open. Paginate large result sets instead of holding every record in memory.

questions.stem: When should a connector throw ConnectorErrorType.NotFound?
choices: In stdAccountRead or stdAccountUpdate, so a missing account is created rather than treated as a failure
During stdAccountList, so missing accounts are reported as errors
On every 403 from the source
When configuration is missing at startup
questions.explanation: NotFound tells SailPoint the account is not on the source. During provisioning, SailPoint then calls std:account:create. Do not use it while listing accounts; a missing account there is simply omitted.

questions.stem: Which error class matches a 403 from the source API?
choices: InsufficientPermissionError
InvalidConfigurationError
InvalidRequestError
TimeoutError
questions.explanation: InsufficientPermissionError is for a 403 or an equivalent access-denied response. InvalidConfigurationError is for bad setup before any API call. InvalidRequestError is for a request the connector cannot build, or a 400 from the source.

questions.stem: What files does a new connector project start with?
choices: index.ts, my-client.ts, and connector-spec.ts
A single XML rule
sp-ui-plugin.json only
A Go module
questions.explanation: index.ts registers commands. my-client.ts is the place for custom API calls when the vendor has no SDK. connector-spec.ts tells SailPoint which commands, config, and schemas the connector has.

questions.stem: What does a connector customizer project contain at the start?
choices: One source file, index.ts, that registers the customizer commands
The same three files as a full connector
A Beanshell rule
An Angular workspace
questions.explanation: A customizer uses the same tools as a connector. The generated project has a single index.ts that registers the customizer commands. You can add more files later.

questions.stem: Where should config.json live relative to git?
choices: In .gitignore, because it holds credentials used to invoke the connector
In the zip you upload, so the tenant can store the token
In the connector spec, as a secrettextarea default
It is optional and can be omitted even when the command requires a key
questions.explanation: config.json is required for CLI invoke tests and must contain at least one key. It holds values such as tokens and passwords, so it belongs in .gitignore.

questions.stem: What is the main reason SailPoint added SaaS Connectivity?
choices: To connect to cloud sources without a virtual appliance, and to build and test the connector locally
To replace every virtual appliance connector, including JDBC
To run IdentityIQ plugins in the cloud
To store connector secrets in the identity profile
questions.explanation: SaaS Connectivity targets cloud sources without a VA. You can develop and debug locally, customize the configuration UI, and use current languages. VA connectivity remains for on-prem sources.

banks.solution: UI plugins and UI Development Kit
banks.topic: UI plugins and UI Development Kit

questions.stem: What has to be true before UI plugin CLI commands will succeed?
choices: The tenant has the experimental feature enabled, and the user has the right for that operation
Any user with a personal access token can create a plugin
A virtual appliance must be connected
The plugin must already be published in CoLab
questions.explanation: UI plugins are experimental and gated. If the feature is off, the backend says it is not enabled for the tenant. Each operation checks its own right, and the CLI names the right you are missing.

questions.stem: Which Node release does the UI plugin starter recommend?
choices: Node 24 or later
Node 18, the SaaS connector minimum
Node 16
No Node, because the starter is Java
questions.explanation: The starter is an Angular application. Node 24 or later is recommended, and the SailPoint CLI must be authenticated to the tenant.

questions.stem: What does init send to the tenant?
choices: Nothing. It scaffolds the workspace and checks the alias, and it does not register the plugin
The manifest, which creates the plugin instance
The compiled assets
A local-dev override for every user
questions.explanation: init scaffolds an Angular workspace, or prepares an existing project, and validates the alias. It does not install dependencies, build, or register. create does the registration.

questions.stem: Which part of sp-ui-plugin.json is stored in the tenant?
choices: Only the manifest; the build section stays local
The whole file, including port and outDir
Only the build section
Neither, because the file is documentation
questions.explanation: The manifest declares the alias, names, scopes, security policy, and slots, and that is what create sends. outDir and port are local CLI settings and are never sent.

questions.stem: What is the lasting identifier of a plugin instance?
choices: The UUID returned by create; the alias is the friendly tenant-unique name
The alias only, which changes when you upload
The local port
The developer's identity id
questions.explanation: create returns a plugin instance id. That UUID is the permanent registration. The alias is the friendly handle and must be unique in the tenant.

questions.stem: Who sees local code after link?
choices: Only the developer who linked, through a per-developer override
Every user in the tenant
Only users listed in restrictToUsers, including people who did not link
Nobody, until upload replaces the instance
questions.explanation: link binds your dev server to your own identity. Other people, and the deployed assets, are unchanged. The tenant shows a Local Dev badge for you. link does not start the dev server.

questions.stem: Which port does link use if you do not pass one?
choices: build.port from the manifest, otherwise 4200
3000, the connector dev server
8081, the event-trigger sample
questions.explanation: The port comes from --port, then build.port, then 4200. The Angular dev server has to already be running on that port.

questions.stem: What does the UI Development Kit do with a client ID already stored by the CLI?
choices: You must enter the client ID and secret again; they are not shared into the kit
It reuses them with no prompt
It rejects PAT authentication
It copies them into the plugin manifest
questions.explanation: The kit uses the CLI's environment shape, but you must re-enter the client ID and secret. You can authenticate with OAuth or a personal access token.

questions.stem: What is the Community Toolbox relative to the UI Development Kit?
choices: The same project
A separate IdentityIQ plugin
The MCP server
The Rule Development Kit
questions.explanation: The UI Development Kit is also the Community Toolbox. Shared components live in projects/sailpoint-components and can be toggled from the component selector.

questions.stem: Where does a local UI Development Kit build land?
choices: The ./release folder, after npm run electron:build
dist, the connector zip folder
The tenant's plugin slot
src/main/resources/rules
questions.explanation: npm run electron:build produces the app for your platform under ./release. Forked GitHub workflows can build macOS, Linux, and Windows copies.

questions.stem: How do you ship a kit build that only opens the transform tool?
choices: Edit app/config.json so the navigation lists only that component
Delete projects/sailpoint-components
Set the plugin to private
Remove the theme picker images
questions.explanation: app/config.json is the default navigation. Limiting it to the transform tool hides the component selector. If a config already exists in the user data directory, the app does not overwrite it.

questions.stem: Where are UI Development Kit theme and user settings stored on Windows?
choices: appData/Roaming/sailpoint-ui-development-kit
The tenant branding API
sp-ui-plugin.json
The virtual appliance keystore
questions.explanation: Theme colors and logos chosen in the theme component are saved under appData/Roaming/sailpoint-ui-development-kit. User settings that turn components on live in that same folder.

questions.stem: What does generate:component add?
choices: A folder under sailpoint-components, a route, a sidebar link, and an export from public-api.ts
A connector command in index.ts
A cloud rule template
An MCP tool
questions.explanation: npm run generate:component creates the component files, registers the component in the selector, adds a route and a sidebar link, and exports it from public-api.ts.

questions.stem: What is the SailPoint CLI command?
choices: sail
spcli
idn
isc
questions.explanation: The CLI is invoked as sail. Prebuilt binaries exist for macOS, Windows, and Linux. The Windows installer is a 64-bit MSI.

questions.stem: How does CLI OAuth sign-in work?
choices: The CLI opens a browser, shows a confirmation code, and you paste back a one-time code that starts with sp1.
You paste a client secret into the browser
The CLI stores your SailPoint password
OAuth works in a pipeline with no terminal
questions.explanation: OAuth uses the authorization code flow with PKCE. The confirmation code on https://developer.sailpoint.com/sailapps must match the CLI. Paste the one-time code only into the CLI that started that sign-in. A pipeline should use a personal access token instead.

questions.stem: What does a tenant name such as acme mean when you configure the CLI?
choices: The CLI uses the identitynow.com domain
The CLI uses identitynow-demo.com
The CLI asks you to type both URLs every time
The name is ignored unless SAIL_BASE_URL is set
questions.explanation: A bare tenant name uses identitynow.com. For any other domain, including a demo tenant, pass the HTTPS URL. You can paste an API URL or a browser URL. sail env update fixes URLs that fail the check.

questions.stem: When can the CLI run without sail env create?
choices: When SAIL_BASE_URL is set
When the tenant name is acme
Only on macOS with Homebrew
Never; an environment file is mandatory
questions.explanation: Environment variables are the way to configure the CLI in CI. If SAIL_BASE_URL is set, you do not need a configured environment. PAT values can come from SAIL_CLIENT_ID and SAIL_CLIENT_SECRET.

questions.stem: Which flag is required on sail search query?
choices: indices
sort
folderPath
wait
questions.explanation: indices is required and names the indices to search. sort is optional; a leading hyphen sorts descending. Results go to search_results in the current directory unless folderPath is set.

questions.stem: What does sail spconfig export do if you leave wait off?
choices: It starts the job and returns without waiting, because wait defaults to false
It waits until the export is COMPLETE
It only prints a template
It imports the folder you pass
questions.explanation: wait defaults to false on export, import, and template. Set it to true to wait and then download. include and exclude choose object types, and download saves a finished job.

questions.stem: How is the Python SDK organized?
choices: By API resource, imported from sailpoint, with the endpoint version on the method name
By a separate package for each API version
As one class that covers every endpoint
As generated Beanshell
questions.explanation: You import a class such as TransformsApi from sailpoint. list_transforms_v1 calls the v1 list endpoint. A second form, list_transforms_v1_with_http_info, also returns status, headers, and raw data.

questions.stem: How do Go SDK method names show the endpoint version?
choices: The version is a suffix, as in ListTransformsV1
You import a v1 or v3 package
The version is a query parameter you set after the call
Go only supports beta endpoints
questions.explanation: Change TransformsAPI to another collection, such as SourcesAPI, and change ListTransformsV1 to another method. The version is part of the method name, not a separate package.

questions.stem: How does the TypeScript SDK avoid a package per API version?
choices: Methods are suffixed with the version, such as listTransformsV1, and you run the example with bun
You install @sailpoint/v1 and @sailpoint/v3 separately
The SDK calls only the latest beta
Version is selected in tsconfig
questions.explanation: Import the resource class, such as TransformsApi, with no version namespace. listTransformsV1 is the v1 list call. The getting-started example runs with bun src/index.ts.

questions.stem: What does the Python example return when it asks for transforms named like Test?
choices: No more than 10 transforms whose names start with Test
Every transform in the tenant
Only internal transforms
A single transform, because the method does not take query parameters
questions.explanation: The getting-started example passes query parameters to list_transforms_v1 so the call returns at most 10 transforms whose names start with Test. The same method without those parameters returns the list the endpoint sends back.

questions.stem: How do you switch the CLI to a personal access token?
choices: sail set pat, then sail set auth pat
sail set auth oauth, then paste the secret in the browser
Export SAIL_BASE_URL only
sail search query with the client id as the query string
questions.explanation: sail set pat prompts for the client ID and secret, masking each character. sail set auth pat selects that method. If the tenant rejects the token, it may be wrong, deleted, or from another tenant.

questions.stem: What does a leading hyphen on a CLI search sort field mean?
choices: Descending order
That the field is required
That the field is excluded
A descending search is not allowed
questions.explanation: sort defaults to ascending. -created sorts that field descending. You can pass more than one sort field, and more than one index.

questions.stem: Where does sail search write results when folderPath is omitted?
choices: A search_results folder in the current working directory
The tenant's report inbox
stdout only, with no file
The spconfig download directory
questions.explanation: Both query and template write JSON into search_results under the current directory unless folderPath points somewhere else. The query goes through the V3 search endpoint.
